newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end mixed, yield curve steepens.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end mixed, yield curve steepens.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed in quiet trade on Friday, with a late rally in the Canadian dollar helping to pull the short end of the yield curve lower, dealers said.

"The currency tested out some interesting technical levels but it's really come back very strongly," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research with TD Securities Inc. "That's helped the short end, so as a result we've seen the curve steepen up a little bit here."
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.02 to C$109.45 to yield 7.195 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond traded unchanged to yield 6.74 percent. The spread between the benchmark bond widened to 46 basis points from 45 basis points at the session's open.

The Canadian dollar, which weakened to as low C$1.3769 (US$0.7316) early in the session, rallied to close at C$1.3699, providing a boost for shorter-term bonds. Dealers said trading in both bond and currency markets was made more volatile by a lack of liquidity.
Canadian bond investors are now looking ahead to U.S. economic data being released next week, including the key employment report, analysts said.
In new issue news, the Government of Canada said it planned to auction on January 8 C$2.7 billion of bonds with a coupon of 5.5 percent and maturing on February 1, 2000.
The new bonds are in addition to C$2.8 billion of the same issue now outstanding and will be issued with accrued interest from October 15, 1996 to January 15, 1997.
The Bank of Canada said it will buy at least C$270 million of the new bonds. The bonds, which will be dated and delivered on January 15, pay interest on February 1 and August 1, the government said.

In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent due 2006 rose C$0.18 to C$103.20 to yield 6.554 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 2/32 to yield 6.51 percent. The spread between the bonds was four basis points.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.90 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.16 percent.
